To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the cyclotrimerization reaction of the corannulyne derivative with the Pd catalyst produced a C60 hydrocarbon with three corannulenic bowls, which prefers a highly noncoplanar C1 conformation with a twist angle of 20°.
the steric hindrance in the highly dissymmetric bowl-to-bowl inverted corannulene molecule tunes the inversion barriers of the corannulene subunits.

the cyclotrimerization reaction of the corannulyne derivative with Pd(PhCN)2Cl2 as catalyst in the presence of triethylamine in toluene at 100 °C produced a hydrocarbon with a highly dissymmetric structure, in which the three corannulenes are twisted with respect to each other and are in different conformations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of corannulynes (C20H10) and their cyclotrimerization, which produced a new C60H24 corannulene trimer.
the synthesis, structural and spectroscopic characterization and the theoretical study of corannulene bowl inversion.
the synthesis and structural studies of a new class of bowl-shaped hydrocarbons with the C60H24 formula.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the steric hindrance of corannulene bowl inversion is a consequence of the steric hindrances of the bowl inversion and pseudorotation.
the steric hindrance inside the corannulenes is responsible for the observed inversion barriers.
the bowl-to-bowl inversion barrier of the corannulyne trimer is the smallest ever observed for a corannulene derivative.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the bowl-to-bowl inversion barrier of the corannulyne trimer can be tuned by the stearic effect of the three corannulenes.
steric effects in the bowl-shaped molecules are not necessarily negligible.
the bowl-to-bowl inversion barrier of the corannulyne trimer is determined by the steric crowding inside the bowl, which in turn is determined by the relative orientation of the subunits.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the inversion barriers of corannulene bowls can be controlled by steric hindrance and the resulting conformational flexibility can be used for the construction of new molecular architectures.
the steric hindrance in a bowl-inclined structure can dramatically tune the inversion barrier.

the bowl inversion barrier of corannulenes, previously thought to be a constant value of about 15 kcal mol–¹, can be tuned by the sterochemistry of their molecular context, thus providing a new tool to control the dynamics of bowl-shaped molecules.
